newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. Air Force plane in safety incidents - Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force plane in safety incidents - Cuba.

text.p: Cuba denounced on Wednesday what it said were incidents last week in which a U.S. Air Force plane flying north of the island came excessively close to two civilian aircraft.

A Cuban armed forces statement in ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma said the incidents Friday involved a U.S. RC-135 plane that was carrying out "exploration against Cuba." The RC-135 is a four-engine tanker that has been modified for reconnaissance uses.

In the first case, the Cuban statement said, a Panamanian DC-8 aircraft flying from Miami to Tocumen in Panama reported to Havana air traffic control on Friday morning that the U.S. Air Force plane had flown dangerously close to it at a point 70 miles (110 km) north of the central province of Ciego de Avila.

The Cuban statement said the U.S. plane flew at an altitude of 30,000 feet (9,000 metres) four miles (six km) from the Compania Panamena de Aviacion plane. It said the altitude difference was 1,500 feet (460 metres) rather than the 2,000 feet (610 metres) required.

Two hours later, the statement said, an American Airlines plane flying from Miami to Cancun, Mexico, reported to Havana air traffic control that it had spotted the same U.S. plane 60 miles (100 km) north of the western province of Pinar del Rio 15 miles (24 km) away. The altitude difference then was 1,000 feet (305 metres), the statement said.
It said Havana air traffic control reported both incidents to air traffic control in Miami. It said there had been 14 close flying incidents involving U.S. planes near Cuba this year.
